title: Why do pea plants keep secrets?

lines.speaker: A
lines.display_text: Hi everyone, welcome back! I'm Meera.
lines.spoken_text: Hi everyone, welcome back! I'm Meera.

lines.speaker: B
lines.display_text: And I'm Arjun. Today we're asking why children look like their parents, but never exactly.
lines.spoken_text: And I'm Arjun. Today we're asking why children look like their parents, but never exactly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.display_text: So where does this story start?
lines.spoken_text: So where does this story start?

lines.speaker: B
lines.display_text: With Mendel and garden pea plants. Peas show clear contrasting traits, like tall plants and short plants. When he crossed a tall plant with a short one, every plant in the first generation, the F1, was tall. None were halfway in between.
lines.spoken_text: With Mendel and garden pea plants. Peas show clear contrasting traits, like tall plants and short plants. When he crossed a tall plant with a short one, every plant in the first generation, called F one, was tall. None were halfway in between.

lines.speaker: A
lines.display_text: Wait, so the short trait just vanished?
lines.spoken_text: Wait, so the short trait just vanished?

lines.speaker: B
lines.display_text: Not quite! When the F1 plants self-pollinated, the F2 generation had tall and short plants in a ratio of about 3:1.
lines.spoken_text: Not quite! When the F one plants self-pollinated, the F two generation had tall and short plants in a ratio of about three is to one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.display_text: A plant with TT or Tt is tall. Only tt gives a short plant.
lines.spoken_text: A plant with capital T capital T, or capital T small t, is tall. Only small t small t gives a short plant.

lines.speaker: A
lines.display_text: So the short trait was hiding, not gone. That's it for today, see you next time!
